rt_dengue

Source: R/rt_dengue.R
rt_dengue.Rd

Effective reproductive number (Rt) of dengue for the country, a state, a municipality or a locality, with the daily incidence of the SINAVE cases and a parametric serial interval ([EpiEstim::estimate_R()]).

rt_dengue(
  dataset,
  level = c("country", "state", "municipality", "locality"),
  place = c("REP", "RES"),
  cve_edo = NULL,
  cve_mpo = NULL,
  cve_loc = NULL,
  status_caso = c(1, 2),
  ref_date = NULL,
  period_days = 365,
  window_days = 21,
  mean_si = 21,
  std_si = 6.1,
  plot = TRUE
)

Arguments

dataset

SINAVE dengue dataset (data.table or data.frame, e.g. read with `data.table::fread("DENGUE2_.txt", quote = "", fill = TRUE)`). It needs `FEC_INI_SIGNOS_SINT`, `ESTATUS_CASO` and, depending on `level` and `place`, `CVE_EDO_*`, `CVE_MPO_*` and `CVE_LOC_*` (`DES_*` give the name of the area).

level

level of analysis: `"country"`, `"state"`, `"municipality"` or `"locality"`.

place

place used to select the cases: `"REP"` place of report (default; the cases are geocoded with it) or `"RES"` place of residence.

cve_edo

INEGI state code (e.g. `"31"` or 31). Required for `"state"`, `"municipality"` and `"locality"`.

cve_mpo

INEGI municipality code (e.g. `"050"` or 50). Required for `"municipality"` and `"locality"`.

cve_loc

INEGI locality code (e.g. `"0001"` or 1). Required for `"locality"`. `cve_mpo` and `cve_loc` can be vectors of the same length (pairs municipality-locality).

status_caso

case status: 1 probable, 2 confirmed (default `c(1, 2)`).

ref_date

reference date (`Date` or `"YYYY-MM-DD"`); NULL (default) uses the latest date of onset of the selected cases.

period_days

days, up to `ref_date`, of the daily incidence used to estimate Rt (default 365).

window_days

days, up to `ref_date`, of the window whose Rt gives the phase of the outbreak (default 21).

mean_si, std_si

mean and standard deviation (days) of the serial interval, gamma distribution (default 21 and 6.1).

plot

logical. If TRUE (default) the Rt curve is printed.

Value

a list (invisibly) with:

rt

object of [EpiEstim::estimate_R()], weekly sliding windows with at least 10 cases; NULL if it cannot be estimated.

rt_ventana

data.frame with the window (`inicio`, `fin`), Rt (`rt`), its 95% credible interval (`rt_inf`, `rt_sup`) and the phase (`fase`).

incidencia

data.frame with the daily incidence (`dates`, `I`).

area

name of the area.

plot

ggplot of the Rt curve (NULL if Rt was not estimated).

Details

By default the area is selected with the place of report of the case (`place = "REP"`), not the place of residence (`"RES"`): in non-endemic areas (e.g. Mexico City) the positive cases are reported in the place where they were exposed, so the place of report is the place of transmission. In endemic areas both give almost the same cases.

Rt is estimated with [EpiEstim::estimate_R()] (Cori et al. 2013), method `"parametric_si"`, on weekly sliding windows with at least 10 cases (curve; with fewer cases the estimate reflects the prior) that start at least `mean_si` + 2 `std_si` days after the first date of onset of the dataset (before it the infectiousness of the previous cases is unknown and Rt is overestimated), and on the window of `window_days` days up to `ref_date`. The phase of the outbreak is given by the 95% credible interval of the Rt of that window: "En ascenso" (lower limit > 1), "En descenso" (upper limit < 1) or "Estable". The last days are usually incomplete (delay of report), which lowers Rt at the end.

References

Cori A, Ferguson NM, Fraser C, Cauchemez S (2013). A new framework and software to estimate time-varying reproduction numbers during epidemics. *American Journal of Epidemiology*, 178(9), 1505-1512.

See also

[EpiEstim::estimate_R()], [mp_active_foci()]

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
dataset <- data.table::fread("DENGUE2_.txt", quote = "", fill = TRUE)

# Mexico
rt_mx <- rt_dengue(dataset = dataset,
                   level = "country",
                   place = "REP",
                   cve_edo = NULL,
                   cve_mpo = NULL,
                   cve_loc = NULL,
                   status_caso = c(1, 2),
                   ref_date = NULL,
                   period_days = 365,
                   window_days = 21,
                   mean_si = 21,
                   std_si = 6.1,
                   plot = TRUE)
rt_mx$rt_ventana

# Acapulco de Juarez (Guerrero), locality 0001 of the municipality 001
rt_aca <- rt_dengue(dataset = dataset,
                    level = "locality",
                    place = "REP",
                    cve_edo = "12",
                    cve_mpo = "001",
                    cve_loc = "0001",
                    status_caso = c(1, 2),
                    ref_date = NULL,
                    period_days = 365,
                    window_days = 21,
                    mean_si = 21,
                    std_si = 6.1,
                    plot = TRUE)
} # }
